clue.text: Material AP submit close to deadline

definitions.note: material in the sense of relevant, pertinent

parts.note: to submit an idea is to posit it

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end of deadline is used

parts.note: its last letter is E

explanation.surface: A news agency's copy is filed just before the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: AP looks like the Associated Press but is simply taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something material to a case is relevant and apt to it, which is what apposite describes.

clue.text: Don't start affair or partnership

indicators.note: the word must not begin, so its opening letter goes

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual love affair

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid beginning a fling or a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or association formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: I only appear out for a music producer

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shy performer says they only show up for a record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music producer' suggests a person in a studio, but it is an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola plays tunes automatically from a perforated roll, so it produces music by itself.

clue.text: Those that could stab heels

definitions.meaning: second meaning: tall narrow shoe heels

explanation.walkthrough: Heels as cads who stab others in the back is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a slim Italian dagger was borrowed for the thin high heel of a woman's shoe.

clue.text: Duds flipping game models modelled

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole of what is built upside down, which in a down clue reads backwards
models in the sense of shapes or frames: the posing word is shaped around the game

parts.note: an artist's model sat for the painter
Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Failed outfits are tossed aside as models parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' here means shapes around: an artist's model sat, and the posing word is wrapped round the board game before the whole is flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Duds is slang for clothes, and togas were the robes worn in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Spooner's computer-aided design plan's rash

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, after Reverend Spooner

parts.note: CAD is the standard abbreviation for computer-aided design
a map is a plan of an area

explanation.surface: An architect's software drawing turns out to be reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: CAD MAP with its initial letters swapped becomes MAD CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap scheme or person is reckless and impulsive, the same idea as rash.

clue.text: See you fuss over independent son

indicators.note: the fuss word reaches over and around the independent letter

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye after making a scene about a free-spirited boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Adios is Spanish for goodbye, a farewell like 'see you'.

clue.text: Energy sources for commercial heavy industry

indicators.note: the source of a word is its beginning, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Power supplies for business and manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's energy sources are power stations; here 'sources' means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese philosophy chi is the vital life force flowing through the body.

clue.text: Fish bar?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rod or bar for a bird to sit on

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fish restaurant or a pub serving fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a spiny freshwater fish and the rod a caged bird rests on.

clue.text: Yen to visit country … Palestine?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the yen letter enters the country

parts.note: Holland is a name for the Netherlands
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A longing to tour a nation in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Palestine as one example of the region so called.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of Palestine is revered as sacred in Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and so is called that.

clue.text: Begging's initially ignored at the front

indicators.note: the opening letter is left out, so the first letter of the begging word is dropped

parts.note: begging is pleading

explanation.surface: Someone notes that begging has been brushed aside from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who is leading is in first place, ahead of the field.

clue.text: One who wanted more food around lunchtime … ham?

definitions.note: a ham is an actor, and the question mark shows this is one example

indicators.note: the boy's name goes round the lunchtime letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Oliver Twist famously asked for more gruel
one o'clock, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A hungry diner around lunch is asked to decide on ham.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated stage actor; 'ham' is crossword slang for an actor, here a playful slight.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a famous English actor, and a ham is a jocular word for any actor.

clue.text: Elegy lass arranged classically

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A poem of mourning is set out for a girl in classical style.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done classically has a timeless quality, never going out of date.

clue.text: Tenor dipped into band's drug supply

indicators.note: the tenor letter is dipped inside the band word

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn across the body

explanation.surface: A singer in a group raids the band's hidden drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stash is a hidden store, often of illicit narcotics.

clue.text: Bitter icon I am sour about

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned about and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone resents a famous figure and admits to being in a foul mood about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrimonious dispute is full of angry resentment, as a bitter one is.

clue.text: Firm bed can make you suffer

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
pit is slang for bed

explanation.surface: A hard mattress can give you a bad night.
explanation.walkthrough: To cop it is British slang for getting into trouble or being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to cop it means to be punished or to get hurt, so to endure pain.

clue.text: One can find slugs in these bedrooms

definitions.text: One can find slugs in these
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... of a gun hold bullets, called slugs
second meaning: an old word for private rooms, bedrooms

explanation.walkthrough: The garden pest is a red herring; slugs are bullets loaded into a revolver.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolver's cylinder has chambers for cartridges, and chamber is also an old word for a private room for sleeping.

clue.text: Catholic quick to have sex in moderation

indicators.note: to have here means to hold within, so the quick word contains the sex word

parts.note: hasty means quick
it is a coy slang word for sex

explanation.surface: A Catholic in a hurry for intercourse is urged to show restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastity is sexual restraint or abstinence, a form of temperance.

clue.text: Reach lowest point pulling a moony obviously!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: prices ... when they stop falling
second meaning: mooning is baring one's backside, so the bottom is out

explanation.walkthrough: A moony is a prank of baring the buttocks; read literally, the phrase describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: When a falling market levels off at its minimum, it is said to have done this.

clue.text: Toilets not working in stalls

parts.note: bogs is British slang for toilets
a system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: Broken lavatories in the cubicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stalls' looks like toilet cubicles, but it is the verb meaning slows or halts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gets stuck and halts progress is said to get mired in this way.

clue.text: On which one might find Derby and Kilmarnock?

definitions.text: On which one might find Derby and Kilmarnock?

parts.words: On which one might find Derby and Kilmarnock?
parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat and a Kilmarnock is a Scottish bonnet, both hung on a coat-room fixture

explanation.walkthrough: Derby and Kilmarnock look like English and Scottish towns or football clubs; both are also kinds of hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallway stand with pegs on which headwear such as bowlers and bonnets is hung.

clue.text: You could say locum has love for speed

parts.note: a locum, a stand-in doctor, could be called a temp
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A stand-in doctor is in love with going fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the pace or rate at which something moves or is played.

clue.text: Philosophical type objects to icing cakes

indicators.note: cakes in the sense of coats or encases: the outer words encase the answer

explanation.surface: A thinker refuses to have frosting on baked goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cakes' looks like the noun after icing, but it is the verb, covering the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic is a follower of the ancient Greek school of Zeno, which taught endurance without complaint.

clue.text: Found time to be sat on by heavenly body

indicators.note: in a down answer the star sits above the time letter, on top of it

parts.note: a star is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: An astronomer found that time is weighed down by a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a business is to establish it, which is to get it going.

clue.text: The sound of cheers in prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: glasses ... when people toast with 'cheers'

explanation.walkthrough: Cheers is the toast, not a crowd's applause.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise of glasses touching in a toast shares its name with a slang word for jail.

clue.text: Burns released them thus honed with edits

indicators.note: editing changes the order of the letters, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer's text is sharpened by revision.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Burns, the boss in The Simpsons, often orders 'Release the hounds!', not the Scottish poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Burns of The Simpsons is known for setting his guard dogs on visitors with that catchphrase.

clue.text: Satellite the French sent up on Ariane (not III, V or VI)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second
in a down clue, sent up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: the Roman numerals are letter positions: the third, fifth and sixth letters are removed

parts.note: the European space rocket

explanation.surface: French engineers launch a moon on one of the Ariane rockets, but not certain models.
explanation.walkthrough: III, V and VI look like Ariane rocket versions but number letters: without its third, fifth and sixth letters ARIANE leaves ARA, under EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Elara is one of the moons of Jupiter, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Assign a use for radios

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the phrase is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; a point is a purpose or use, as in 'what's the point?'

explanation.surface: Someone gives a purpose to wireless sets.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to name or allot them to a role or task.

clue.text: Tailed fruit or vegetable

indicators.note: tailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Asking whether a produce item with a tail counts as fruit or vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is a small green seed eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Drink in Guam or Osorno

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of the place names

explanation.surface: A drink is ordered on a Pacific island or in a Chilean city.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoroso is a sweet, dark style of sherry.

clue.text: Big star in Cheers

parts.note: the 1988 film Big starred Tom Hanks; T is the initial of his first name
Hanks, the surname of the film's leading actor

explanation.surface: A famous actor appeared in the sitcom set in a Boston bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers looks like the TV series; here it is British slang for gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain cheers is an informal way of expressing gratitude.

clue.text: One punching sick Spartan fighter

indicators.note: the one letter punches its way into the middle of the jumbled word
sick suggests something out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone hits an ill warrior from ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a member of an irregular armed resistance force.
